newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary heavy-weight shrs fall, pull BUX down.
newsitem.headline: Hungary heavy-weight shrs fall, pull BUX down.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange came down from Monday's surprising rally in what market participants described as a natural follow-up and which does not give reason for any panic.
The BUX index finished at 5,803.26 points, down 98.78 points or 1.67 percent.
"The clear reason behind today's fall was Monday's too sharp rally," said Peter Lencs of MKB Securities. "I don't see any major problem behind."
Traders said Wall Street had less impact on the market than before.
"The Hungarian market was quite well correlated to the Dow Jones recently, now this seems to be a little over," he said.
BUX futures fell for all maturities, by between 58 points and 124 points. June BUX closed at 6,142 points, down 58.00, while December 1998 BUX lost 110 points to 8,060.
"Longer-term maturities usually fall more than nearer ones while in the opposite case they tend to rise steeper: basically that's what we saw today," Lencs said.
Analysts said foreign investors were mostly in a wait-and-see attitude looking forward to see a clear market trend.
"They are on the sidelines," said Nigel Rendell, emerging markets strategist at HSBC James Capel in London. "They're waiting to see if a more significant trend or direction on the market emerges."
The market's long-term outlook, however, remains bullish.
"There might be a little bit of up and down in the short-term but I'm still confident that we are going to see the index quite a bit higher by the end of the year," Rendell said.
On Tuesday heavy-weigth stocks lost ground, with chemicals TVK falling 110 forints to 2,710 and oil company MOL dropping 70 to 3,225.
Hotel firm Danubius finished at 5,700 forints, down 185, but at a certain point it traded at a daily low of 5,290.
Packaging company Cofinec rose 160 forints to 5,160, after Nomura Equity Research rated its Global Depositary Receipts as "buy".
